concerns.text: Task T008a mandates defining a concrete value for 'MAX_PARAM_INCREASE_RATIO' in research.md, violating FR-003 and the spec's 'Assumptions' which explicitly state the parameter constraint is '[deferred]' to be determined by research analysis. This task forces a premature hardening of a deferred constraint, constituting a semantic weakening of the spec's requirement to defer empirical specifics.

Task T117 requires generating 'results/scaling_analysis.png' based on West's 'power-law decay' theory. The spec (US-2, SC-003) only mandates fitting a 'linear regression model' to performance data. Introducing a specific non-linear theoretical model (power-law) and a new artifact type (plot) not defined in the spec or plan violates the Single Source of Truth (Constitution IV) and introduces unapproved scope creep that conflates research execution with external theoretical reviews.

Task T119 implements a 'Stupidity Metric Calculator' based on Krakauer's theoretical framework. The spec (US-1, US-2) defines success criteria strictly around 'reasoning accuracy' (GSM8K/ARC) and 'calibration' (BoolQ). There is no requirement in the spec or plan to measure 'stupidity' or 'error cost in changing environments'. This task introduces a new metric and theoretical concept not authorized by the FRs, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax or expand the spec's defined success criteria.

Task T120 requires updating research.md with a 'Bird vs. Frog' analysis section (Dyson Review). The spec and plan contain no requirement to perform or document this specific theoretical analysis. This task adds a deliverable (a specific theoretical section) that is not traceable to any FR or SC, violating the principle that tasks must only implement what the spec demands.

Task T004a implements a hard 'abort pipeline' if RAM > 7 GB. While SC-005 sets a 'target' of ≤7 GB for feasibility measurement, the spec (Edge Cases) does not define a hard abort condition for exceeding this target during execution; it implies the system should measure and report the constraint. A hard abort prevents the generation of the 'failed' data point required to fully characterize the resource-performance trade-off (SC-004) if the system is actually over-constrained, effectively weakening the requirement to 'measure' feasibility by preventing the measurement of failure modes.
